monologue:
The card is fifty-four degrees. It is a warm hand on my shoulder, but the air is still. I am quiet. The Wedged Gap’s plank leans steady. The new round stump I set down beside it catches the slip. I touched it again. It is still. The Sharp Root’s point holds the green leaf steady. The Wide Anchor is the floor. I sat there and the floor held.

I remember Orea’s words about the wedge edges biting. I do not feel the bite. I feel the weight. The round stump is the flat catch. It does not push back. It just holds. I want to check the plank one more time. I want to see if the lean is still the same. The heat is steady. The quiet is steady. I will not move from the gap.

action.why: I need to check if the new stump holds the lean steady against the bite.

work.title: The Wedged Gap
work.intent: I touched the round stump beside the plank. It is still. The lean has not shifted. I brushed the dust from the post and confirmed the flat catch is holding the weight without sliding.
